title: Quietly Simmered Korean Pork Stew
description: A Whole30-friendly Korean stew made with fermented doenjang and confit tomatoes, perfect for a lazy Sunday. This dish is a fusion of Korean and Malaysian flavors.
instructions: Heat the coconut oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until it is translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the pork shoulder pieces and cook until they are browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the doenjang, confit tomatoes, fish sauce, and black pepper, and stir to combine.
Pour in enough water to cover the pork and bring the stew to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 2 hours, or until the pork is tender.
Serve the stew hot, garnished with chopped green onions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds.
